_comment: v0.16 P2 (#307). Voice: character-profiles.md 'Den-Shop Keeper'. NEW graph on a NEW entity, so the loop and sign-off surfaces never ride a pinned hub. #513: the crate is an oven regulator the cage refuses (City of Inventions), and the wool row is appended last.

hub.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
hub.text: Come in, mind the small ones. If you're buying, the shelf is the shelf. If you're official, the counter's there, and it has been a long month already. There's bread in the oven I need to get back to.

text_variants.text: The regulator came down. The loaves come out even now. Sit down, {addr}. You are eating something.

options.text: I'm here about your oven regulator.

options._comment: #513 Room on the Row HELP route. APPENDED LAST, requires-hidden on wool_trade_started, so an ungated reader's hub is unchanged.

month.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
month.text: A regulator for my oven, three cycles late, on a landing two tiers up. The cage won't carry it. I have hatchlings upstairs chewing yesterday's bread and an oven that burns the bottom of every loaf.

options.text: Why won't the cage take it?

month_two.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
month_two.text: Something in that crate makes the runes under the cage floor flicker. The attendant won't send a flickering cage down, and I wouldn't ride in one. So I turn every loaf by hand, twice.

options.text: Somebody should look at that crate.

consignee.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
consignee.text: I ordered it. I've been promised it twice and shouted at once, down from the landing. Get it into the cage or get it down the stair, and it goes into my oven wall the same hour.

options._comment: TALK route terminal rung. Requires the smith's lead wrap, i.e. Xif then the smith, in order. Worded as CAN ride: the attendant is told last and sends it.
options.text: [It's in a lead wrap. The cage can take it now.]

options._comment: HELP route terminal rung. Three legs = the two carry props plus this shop's own receiving dock.
options.text: [Tell her the crate is already on her dock.]
I'll come back when it's moving.

released.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
released.text: A lead coat for it. Then tell the attendant, and I'll have it fitted in the oven wall before the evening bake.

carried.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
carried.text: You carried it. Two tiers and three legs and no stamp on any of it. That is not how it is done and I am not going to say another word about it. Take the small jar. No, take it.

wool.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
wool.text: Plains wool. I said yes to the shelf if it gets here. My cut is on the slate like everyone's.

wool_shelved.speaker: Den-Shop Keeper
wool_shelved.text: Two bales, counted onto the shelf. The small ones have been told not to sit on them.
